author: UserAnnon9
title: Fun game, too much pressure to spend
content:
I genuinely loved this game, but the higher you get in levels, the more it feels like you’re being pushed to spend real money just to keep progressing. Buying cash, gems, and chips starts to feel less optional and more necessary. After a certain level, you barely get enough resources to keep your businesses going without constantly needing more.

The gems, chips, and cash are also extremely expensive for the small amounts you receive in return. When doing HUSTLE challenges, it seems like the casino games stop giving you what you need when you’re close to completing them, almost as if you’re being pushed to buy more. The games are usually very consistent until you’re near the end of a challenge, which makes it much harder to actually complete one without spending money.

The same thing happens with the Collect-It cards. When you’re close to completing a set, you stop getting new cards and just receive the same old cards over and over. The duplicates help you build up enough gems to buy a wildcard, but it feels like we’re really being pushed to purchase wildcards with real money instead.

It’s the same pattern with the pets. Once you run out of chips, there’s really nothing left to do. I thought the update might improve some of these issues, but now we can eat pizza—which we have to pay for—and get nothing back from it.

It’s just obnoxiously obvious that we’re being pushed to spend money. I don’t have a problem with spending money on a game, especially one I enjoy, but when the game itself isn’t improving and we get so little in return for what we buy, spending money starts to feel pointless.

author: KamieW
title: Misleading Ads, Stalled Progress & Serious Concerns.
content:
I’ve been playing Sunday City for almost a year, and during that time I’ve watched the game change drastically some changes were good, but unfortunately, a lot of them have made the game much less enjoyable.

One of my biggest issues is that I never received prizes I earned for inviting other people to the game. Then, during one of the updates, players lost levels and ranking progress, which made reaching the next status even harder. When I contacted support about it, I was basically told that the changes were made to make the game “better” for everyone. From a player’s perspective, it definitely has not felt better.

I have also been stuck at level 4464 for months with absolutely no way to expand or progress further. In order to reach the next level, I need to increase my rank, but the developers have not added any new personal jobs for me to build that would actually allow me to raise that rank. So I’m essentially stuck — not because I haven’t played enough or completed what I’m supposed to, but because the game has not provided the content necessary for me to move forward. After investing nearly a year into a game, being unable to progress for months because the necessary features simply haven’t been added is incredibly frustrating.

At the same time, the game feels increasingly designed to push players into spending real money just to enjoy it or make reasonable progress. Events and tasks have become extremely difficult to complete without purchasing additional items or resources. On top of that, there are often several different side quests and mini-games happening at the same time, all requiring different resources, which makes earning what you need even more difficult. It honestly feels intentional — like the goal is to frustrate players into paying.

The glitches are another major problem. The Jetski game, in particular, glitches terribly and can make an already difficult event even more frustrating.

What also bothers me is the advertising. Almost every Sunday City ad I’ve seen on social media shows gameplay and freedom that simply do not exist in the actual game. The ads make it look like players can freely make choices and interact with the world in ways that we cannot actually do.

There are many more issues I could mention, but after playing for nearly a year, I’m reaching the point where my family and I will probably be looking for another game. I genuinely enjoyed Sunday City before, which is what makes the direction the game has taken so disappointing.

Another issue that has become increasingly uncomfortable is the lack of representation and the way Black characters seem to be treated compared with the white characters in the game. There is only one Black chat character while there are several white characters, and nearly every new character skin I’ve seen added has been for a white woman or white man, while the Black characters continue to be overlooked with little to no meaningful updates. Even the clothing options have raised concerns — at one point, clothing for a Black female character displayed the word “LOSER,” which was later changed to “LOVE.” On top of that, I have seen players allowed to use usernames that were obvious plays on racial slurs (Nate Higgers), which should never make it through moderation. That is especially concerning because, although the game is rated 18+, it appears that many younger players are active in the chats, and some of the conversations I’ve seen there are extremely inappropriate and disturbing. The developers need to take representation, moderation, and the safety of younger users much more seriously.

I hope the developers start listening to longtime players, fix the ongoing glitches, honor rewards that players earn, add the content necessary for longtime players to actually continue progressing, and focus more on making the game enjoyable instead of making every feature feel like another attempt to get players to spend money.

More unusual pets! I would love to see things like hedgehogs, foxes, otters, ducks, penguins, red pandas, squirrels, or even a little colorful parrot running around with us.
Expand the city! Those roadblocks are just sitting there teasing us. Give us somewhere new to go eventually!

author: Rosebuddx97
title: My honest review as a binge player
content:
I’ve been playing this game for just about a month now, and honestly, there are a few things that myself and other players have noticed that we really wish could be improved.

One thing that doesn’t make much sense to me is the pricing for venues and private parties. Why is it only 70 gems to rent a venue, but 200 gems to actually throw a party? Personally, I think it would make more sense for the venue to cost around 100 gems and the party itself to be around 50 gems.

It’s already difficult to earn gems without purchasing them, so lowering the cost of parties would give players more opportunities to actually host parties and join more private parties. The gem packs are also expensive when you consider that it can cost around $10 USD just to have enough gems for one party. Not everyone can afford to spend that kind of money on a game, and players shouldn’t feel like they have to spend real money just to participate and have fun.

Making private parties more affordable would allow players to host and join them more often, have more fun, and have more opportunities to participate in and win tournaments. Right now, some players don’t even get that opportunity because they can get knocked out by higher-level players who are able to bet much higher amounts.

I also think there should be a way for party hosts to see whether the players they are inviting to a private party actually have enough gems to participate. There are unfortunately a lot of scammers on this game, and having some type of verification or indicator would help protect hosts and players from wasting their time and resources on people who aren’t actually able to participate.

Another feature I would love to see is the ability to trade or exchange duplicate gold cards from card packs that we’ve already completed. Even if there is a second-skin option available, I still think players should have a limited window — even just a few hours — to trade their duplicate gold cards with other players who still need them. This would give those cards more value and help players work together to complete their packs without making the trading system unlimited.

I also think this would make a huge difference for new players, especially those who genuinely enjoy the game but don’t want to feel like they have to spend real money just to level up or keep up with other players. Making progression and events more accessible would give newer players more of a reason to stick around and become part of the community.

Another thing I would really love to see is an expanded friends list and a larger group limit. Sometimes our groups are much bigger than four people. Personally, I’m usually playing with at least eight friends at a time, and we all want to play together. With the current group limit, it’s next to impossible to get everyone into the same server without constantly trying to teleport people around.

Overall, I really enjoy this game and the community I’ve found through it. These are just some suggestions that I think could make the experience even better, especially for new players and people who enjoy playing with larger groups of friends. I hope the developers will consider some of these changes because I’d genuinely love to see this game continue to grow.

author: Toibylaw
title: My Favorite Life-Simulation Game
content:
I absolutely love Sunday City! It has quickly become my number-one go-to game. It is usually the first game I open on my device, and I can easily play for hours completing quests, missions, mini-games, and working my way up.

I especially love the small-community feel and the combination of life simulation, role-playing, and time-management. It gives me some of the freedom and interaction I enjoy in games like The Sims or GTA, but without feeling overly aggressive, violent, or stressful.

My main suggestion would be to add more quests, missions, locations, cities, and activities so there is always something new to work toward. I also wish limited-time events gave players more opportunities to earn the specific items needed to participate. For example, during the recent blackjack tournament, the black-and-yellow tokens were difficult to obtain. When an event only lasts a few days, the required tokens or chips should be more readily available through completing quests, opening reward boxes, watching videos, collecting machine rewards, receiving gifts, or making optional purchases.

Overall, Sunday City is an amazing game with so much potential to become even bigger and better. I genuinely look forward to the daily refresh of my chips and coins so I can continue playing. Please keep expanding the game because I would love to see more cities, missions, events, and ways to explore!

author: SheffInTheKitchen
title: Predatory Game Tactics
content: At first glance, the game seems like fun. A sims style premise with decent customization draws you in. But after the early hours pass, and you level up, you see  it for what it is: a glorified promotion for gambling. EVERYTHING is this “life sim” goes through casinos. Everything you do is to earn chips to go use in the casinos. Remodeling costs are astronomical the more you level up, forcing you to scramble for more chips. The whole endgame seems to be to get you to spend real money. Anytime you run out of one of the three currencies, you get THREE back to back to back ads to buy more!! It’s really a well crafted effort to glorify gambling. Good activities, great graphics, and a decent size world. But progress far enough and the illusion fades away.

author: Polymorphous187
title: A Black-Box Casino Disguised as a Life Simulator
content:
Sunday City starts out feeling generous. Wins come frequently, bonus rounds trigger often, and the first few businesses progress quickly enough to make the game seem reasonably balanced.

Then the wall hits.

By the fourth business, upgrade costs increase dramatically and progression slows to a crawl. Businesses generate chips, but upgrades require money, and the resources you earn do not scale anywhere close to the rising cost of progression.

The developers have responded to similar criticism by saying progression simply takes time, but that misses the actual problem. Either the game’s economy was poorly designed and its systems do not scale together, or it was deliberately designed to make normal progression increasingly impractical without more frequent in-game purchases.

Because businesses mainly generate chips rather than the money needed for upgrades, players are heavily funneled into the slot machines. You must wager those chips and hope the game awards enough payouts, bonus rounds, job tokens, and cashback to continue progressing.

The “Jobs” system also does not meaningfully affect progression in the way some advertisements imply. Jobs mainly provide supplemental money for businesses and additional chips, which are then gambled in hopes of earning more money and job tokens. Much like the businesses themselves, job rewards do not appear to scale at the same rate as progression. Instead, the game pressures players to accelerate their job levels—and obtain the resources tied to higher levels—through in-game purchases.

Every other supplemental source of resources follows essentially the same structure. Combined, the free rewards amount to only minutes of meaningful gameplay.

What makes this worse is that the developer does not publish the payout percentages. There is no disclosed RTP, bonus frequency, jackpot probability, job-token drop rate, or explanation of whether the odds are fixed and identical for every account.

That makes the game’s economy impossible to evaluate honestly. Players can spend real money on virtual currency, wager it through what is effectively a black-box casino, and receive no meaningful information about the expected return or their chances of obtaining anything useful for progression.

Regardless of whether it meets the legal definition of gambling in a particular jurisdiction, it uses many of the same psychological mechanisms: variable rewards, jackpots, loss chasing, timed events, artificial scarcity, and paid currency replenishment.

The early game feels designed to establish the habit and make meaningful progression seem achievable. The later game increasingly consumes either your time or your money. Until the developers publish the actual payout percentages and clarify whether the odds are fixed and identical for every player, I strongly recommend against spending money on Sunday City.

In my view, this type of game is predatory. It deliberately combines opaque gambling mechanics, artificial progression barriers, and real-money purchases in a way that gives players almost no ability to judge what they are actually buying. Systems like this deserve far greater scrutiny and regulation, and frankly, I question whether they should be legal at all.

author: NRBEKE
title: Truly Wish I Could Give 5 Stars!
content:
There’s a difference between developers who make a game… and developers who pour themselves into creating an experience. This game feels like it was built by people who genuinely love the art of building games.

What makes this game stand out isn’t just the gameplay — it’s the intention behind it. Every detail feels like it was designed with the player in mind. There’s a clear understanding of user experience, pacing, reward systems, and the small moments that make players smile. It’s rare to find a game that feels both thoughtfully engineered and genuinely charming.

The developers have created something that feels effortless from the player’s perspective, but that actually requires an incredible amount of creativity and attention to detail behind the scenes. The balance is impressive: enough daily engagement to keep you excited, but not so demanding that it starts feeling like a second job. It respects the player’s time while still giving them reasons to come back.

Even the ad system deserves recognition because it’s one of the smartest implementations I’ve seen in a mobile game. Instead of interrupting the experience, ads are positioned as optional opportunities. Players feel like they’re making a choice: “Do I want this extra boost?” rather than “I have to watch this.” That distinction matters. It’s a genuinely clever example of understanding player psychology while still maintaining trust.

The amount of personality, creativity, and tiny unexpected details throughout the game shows that this wasn’t just built to fill a market gap, it feels like it was built by people who actually care about what players experience.

This is the kind of game that reminds you there are still developers out there who understand that great games aren’t just about mechanics. They’re about creating a world players want to return to on a consistent basis. 

That being said, I only have three complaints/suggestions:

1. The world needs more rotation and variety. For a game intentionally designed for long-term engagement, staying in the same city for so long eventually becomes repetitive. This is actually the exact reason I stopped playing for almost six months before coming back. The potential for themed city rotations is huge. Imagine a futuristic Sunday City with alien encounters and special missions, or a rodeo-themed Sunday City with horses, cowboy events, and unique challenges. Monthly or seasonal transformations would keep longtime players excited and give the game a fresh identity over time.

2. The level progression becomes painfully slow later on. The beginning progression feels perfectly paced, but once you reach the higher levels, the wait between milestones becomes a serious grind. Instead of only relying on longer waits, I think adding more mid-range jobs or activities would help. After months of playing, the same tasks start feeling repetitive. More variety would make the grind feel like progress instead of repetition.

3. The forced social interaction update was a mistake (in my opinion). One of the things I loved most about this game was that it respected different types of players. You could enjoy the game independently without needing constant interaction with strangers. Recently, though, new features have made social interaction feel required, like needing to visit another player’s apartment, to earn high-value chips and complete daily tasks.

For players who enjoy that social aspect, great! But for gamers who are online introverts, it changes the entire experience. Having to ask strangers for help, add people you don’t know, and rely on those interactions to complete daily goals makes the game feel less welcoming. It turns an optional feature into a requirement, which takes away some of the freedom that made the game special.

Overall, this is still one of the most thoughtfully designed mobile games I’ve played. The creativity, attention to detail, and player-focused design are obvious. I just hope future updates remember what made the game so enjoyable in the first place: letting players choose how they want to play.

author: Mama-Bear Meghan
title: Listen to the community
content:
I’ve enjoyed playing Sunday City, but there are several features that need improvement.

First, why don’t our apartments have a restroom? It would make the apartments feel much more complete and realistic. We also need more customization options. Players should be able to change their clothes, skin tone, body shape, hairstyle, and other appearance features whenever they want instead of having such limited options.

Getting a pet is also more difficult than it should be because we’re only allowed to save a limited amount of pet food. This makes caring for pets feel unnecessarily restrictive.

Another disappointment is that part of the casino still isn’t open. Many players have been waiting for more content, but it hasn’t been made available yet.

The developers really need to listen to the community. Players have been providing feedback and suggestions, but it often feels like they’re being ignored. If these concerns aren’t addressed, people will eventually move on to other games. I want to give Sunday City a higher rating because it has a lot of potential, but it’s hard to leave a positive review when the player feedback doesn’t seem to be heard.

author: Lauren630048101
title: This game is my new favorite
content:
After playing this game for over a month, I wanted to write a thoughtful review. 

Pros: 
This game is absolutely well made. You can tell a lot of thought goes into the events and gameplay itself. The world and city itself are amazing, I love the addition of the apartment and I hope to see more additions like this in the future! I like the cars as well and I like that you can play for free or spend money to get rewards needed. I like the businesses and I like how when you level up things get easier like the business prices. 
I like that you can also choose what ads you are interested in! I also love the unique pets and look forward to more unique animals!

Cons:
** update went to sleep at 2am with 45 minutes left on the apartment cozy shop change. Woke up at 8 am and now I have 23 hours and 59 minutes. 6 hours went by so this should be at like 18 hours or something right? Please fix!**
The game is great so these cons are just being nit picky at this point, but I do think it could make game play a lot better. 
With the new apartment, I noticed that the cozy store only refreshes 1 every 24 hours, which is a long time for 5 items, especially when it refreshes you can get the same item again which then I wait even longer for new items. 
I also noticed that the timing for things is laggy or sometimes changed. For example I wanted 24 hours for the store or saw that 6 days was left on the cards then changed to a later time. This can create frustration or confusion. Since I am already planning on the next thing. One thing that could be enhanced is if you have a private party, the circle for the party could just be the whole room so that all people don’t have to squish together haha
Also… when having new characters in the game, it would be a small but amazing addition to add a new avatar icon with the new character! Small things make the biggest difference!

Thank you for an amazing game!

author: RealifeAllly
title: Fun game but not Freeplay
content:
I enjoy playing Sunday City, but I think the game has a lot of potential for improvement. The career challenge system can feel repetitive, and I’d love to see more freedom in how players progress. Instead of being limited to specific challenges, it would be great if players could choose their own career paths, start different business ventures, and build their lives the way they want while still having side jobs available to earn extra money.

Another feature I’d love to see is more character customization. Right now, everyone looks very similar, and the game is missing a sense of individuality. Giving players more options to personalize their appearance would make the experience feel more immersive and unique.

Overall, it’s a fun game with a solid foundation, but adding more freedom, career choices, and customization would make it much more engaging and enjoyable long-term.
